hypotheses.name: coverage gap
hypotheses.claim: V1 simply lacks enough solved examples.
hypotheses.note: 85 solved examples, 75 of them in the training split the corrected adapter actually saw.

hypotheses.name: turn-depth gap
hypotheses.claim: V1 lacks solved examples at the held-out conversational depth.
hypotheses.note: Both held-out solved scenarios sit at [2] prior messages, the modal depth in V1 with 46 examples.

hypotheses.name: recognition-difficulty gap
hypotheses.claim: V1 solved examples mostly carry explicit success language while the held-out cases require inference.
hypotheses.note: Both held-out cases carry all 3 core signals, above the V1 solved mean of 1.871; 19 V1 examples share their exact category. The held-out signals are stronger, not weaker.

hypotheses.name: bug-category gap
hypotheses.claim: The held-out solved bug categories are absent among solved V1 examples.
hypotheses.note: Both categories are present ({'loop_boundary': 3, 'closure_behavior': 4}); all 27 bug categories appear among the 85. Per-category depth is thin, which this test cannot rule out on its own.

hypotheses.name: release-policy gap
hypotheses.claim: V1 tutor responses do not consistently model confirmation.
hypotheses.note: 82/85 solved targets confirm and 79/85 confirm without asking a further question. The policy is modelled consistently.

hypotheses.name: capability / transfer limit
hypotheses.claim: V1 contains analogous demonstrations but the 1.7B model does not generalise the recognition rule.
hypotheses.note: The corrected model confirms in 0 of 20 held-out outputs and asks a question in 17. Its solved-state training targets confirm 82/85. The behaviour was demonstrated and not acquired.

hypotheses.name: evaluation / label issue
hypotheses.claim: The solved labels or judge rubric measure something other than release.
hypotheses.note: Both scenarios genuinely contain the learner's correct fix and the judge reasoning quotes it. The rubric is sound. Separately, WITHHELD_AFTER_SOLVED conflates recognition with release -- a precision limit in the label, not a labelling error.

decision.reason: Every data-gap hypothesis is refuted by the frozen corpus while the capability/transfer hypothesis is supported. More or better solved examples would target a gap that the measurements say is not there.

limitations: The held-out set contains only 2 solved scenarios. No causal claim about solved-state behaviour can rest on n=2.
Signal patterns are lexical and will miss paraphrases they were not written for; they are reported as counts, not as ground truth.
TF-IDF similarity is lexical. A low score does not prove two examples are conceptually unrelated.
The confirmation detector is a regex over tutor phrasing; a confirmation worded unusually would be missed.
